input.summary:
Stair lobby furnished in parts/room-3.mjs: hall table with standing lantern by the flight 1 foot, bench (dark_oak_stairs) on the west wall, three letterbox trapdoors on the east wall, hanging lantern under the landing floor.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines for this part; `mcd room --only "stair lobby"` says OK, walk ok, light min 8 with 0 dark cells.
Door first cells (x23..24 z18, x24..25 z15) and the flight 1 foot and head stay clear; no stairs built by this part.
left: Only two lanterns plus the letterboxes; the room is small, so it reads sparse. Enough for the light rule, not rich.
Letterboxes are dark_oak_trapdoor because barrel is not in palette.json; there is no carpet block in the palette, so no rug.
`mcd rooms --out room.png` shows only the roof-top exterior of the stair bay, so the interior furniture could not be checked by eye; the room check's text grid is the evidence instead.

`mcd room` walk lists 4 floor cells at y10 (above the letterbox trapdoors at x25 and the table lantern at x22 z17) as unreached; these are the tool counting tops of non-air blocks as floor, and the verdict is still OK.
plan.md's Notes and the elements checklist were not edited (no room-3 item in elements.md; the Light item stays for the lamplighter pass).

companions.task: confirm the flight 1 foot at x22..23 z15 and its head clearance before anyone places furniture near it; they are locked by the joiner, so a check, not a build.

the room is lit at min 8 with two lanterns; a second look at whether the hanging lantern can sit over the lane centre line in the bay shell, and whether a lantern on the street-door side would help the entrance read at night.
a proper letter rack or parcel shelf on the east wall for the letterboxes, since barrels are not in the palette and the trapdoors read as flaps only.

waste.what: Placed the furniture by hand as layers() text and got a column offset wrong (table leg and top one column east), found only after reading the draft back.
waste.cost: 3 Edit retries, about 2 minutes of the 12.
waste.tool: layers() could print the cell list it wrote as world coordinates (x,y,z=block) on request, or `mcd plan --rooms` could print the column ruler (x22 x23 x24 x25) above each layer so the text layout is checked before writing.

waste.what: Worked out the door first cells, the flight 1 foot and its head clearance and the lane from the plan grid and plan.md by hand.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of reasoning, no coordinate script.
waste.tool: `mcd plan --rooms --only <room>` could mark keep-clear cells (doorway first cells, stair foot and head from the locked flight) as 'k' so the designer draws around them without re-deriving.

waste.what: Palette has no barrel or carpet, which the trade wants for letterboxes and rugs; I substituted trapdoors and skipped the rug.
waste.tool: palette.json could list barrel and a carpet role (dark_oak/white carpet) under objects for interior rooms.

waste.what: The room render shows only the roof-top exterior, so the interior was not visible by eye; I relied on the text light and walk grids.
waste.tool: `mcd rooms --only <room>` could default to a cutaway (roof and walls above the room removed) so the furniture is visible from above.
